subject: MAP: cost sanity sprint — tokens/$ checks
messages:
From: Jordan Peters <jordan@aureliahealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurelia Health Procurement <purchasing@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: cost sanity sprint — tokens/$ checks

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has asked us to lock down the MAP economics section before we sign the SOW — specifically a short, testable checklist for token economics (tokens/$), caching assumptions, and batching behavior under our traffic profile.

I attached the traffic_profile we promised (a CSV with per-endpoint qps and percentiles). Our procurement deadline is 2025-06-12 — can your team run a lightweight verification pass and give us:
- a short runbook of what you tested,
- a few sensitivity numbers (tokens per response, expected tokens/$ under our 95th pct traffic), and
- any gating items that would block the close or require a pricing exception.

We don't need a full audit, just evidence we can present to finance and the legal team.

Thanks,
Jordan Peters
Director, Product @ Aurelia Health

Attachment: aurelia_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Peters <jordan@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: cost sanity sprint — tokens/$ checks

Jordan — thanks for the profile, got it. We're happy to run a focused MAP econ sanity sprint. Proposed plan / timeline: 

1) 6/4 (today) — align on acceptance gates and required artifacts.
2) 6/5 — run smoke sims (three scenarios: baseline, high-burst, prefix-caching).
3) 6/6 — deliver a short summary (1–2 pages) with tokens/$ estimates, sensitivity table, and any proposed SOW redlines for pricing or fallback variants.

Deliverables we'll produce: MAP-draft-v1.docx (econ checklist + runbook), sim-results-preview.csv (summary of token counts & latency distributions), and a short readout slide.

Questions / asks for procurement:
- Confirm whether the 99th pct latency SLO needs to be included in the econ worksheet (adds constraints to batching).
- Share a representative prompt set for the three endpoints (prompt length matters a lot for tokens/$).

I'll kick off the sims and loop Neha and Ben for the engineering/ops checks. If you need the readout sooner than 6/6 tell me and we'll compress.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Strategic Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.docx (stubbed), aurelia_traffic_profile.csv (forwarded)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>

On Wed, Jun 4, 2025 at 11:04 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the profile, got it. We're happy to run a focused MAP econ sanity sprint. Proposed plan / timeline: 
> ...

Quick technical assumptions and plan from my side (so the sims are reproducible and procurement sees the exact inputs):

Assumptions (will document in MAP-draft-v1):
- Model variant for sims: redwood-30b-quant (best tradeoff for this workload).
- Average prompt tokens (per request): 150 (customer-provided prompt sets will adjust this).
- Average response tokens: 300 (most endpoints return ~200–400 tokens).
- Average tokens per call: 450 (prompt + response).
- KV/prefix cache expected hit-rate: 30% baseline. With prefixing campaign we can bump to ~55% for stabilized conversational flows.
- Batching: target micro-batch size = 16 for cost sims. Latency SLOs: 95th <= 220ms; 99th <= 350ms. If procurement requires 99th <= 200ms we must reduce batch size to 4–8 and recalc cost.
- Cost constants (approx): $0.00012 per 1k tokens at current reserved profile (internal estimate) => ~2.7 tokens/$? (we'll provide full tokens-per-dollar table after sims).

Planned sims (to be attached as sim-results-preview.csv):
- Baseline: current profile, 30% cache, batching16, nominal token distribution.
- Burst: 2x 95th percentile, batching fallback to 4 when latency > SLO.
- Prefix-cache uplift: evaluate improvements at 55% hit-rate (look at marginal token reduction and effective tokens/$).

Gating items that block close (short list to show procurement):
- If the customer's average prompt tokens are >250, cost per active user increases ~25–40% vs our baseline assumptions.
- If procurement requires strict 99th latency that forces batch size <8, normalized tokens/$ will rise significantly (we'll quantify).
- If they need on-prem private deployment with dedicated capacity, pricing needs a different reserved commit (we'll flag).

I'll attach a preview CSV of the sim run and the script parameters. If Jordan can share a small representative prompt set (5–10 prompts per endpoint) I will rerun sims with real prompts and update numbers.

Attachment: sim-results-preview.csv (summary stub)

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
ML Engineer, Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Peters <jordan@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 14:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: cost sanity sprint — tokens/$ checks

Thanks team — this readout and the assumptions look good to me. I'll run a quick smoke sim (baseline + prefix uplift) on our reserved pool now and attach the output to the MAP-draft-v1 before we send to Aurelia.

Two operational notes for procurement:
- We'll include a fallback model variant (redwood-13b-quant) in the MAP if they want a cheaper price floor.
- If procurement asks for a pricing cap we should propose a usage band (e.g., up to 2M tokens/mo at X price, tiered thereafter) rather than a hard cap — easier to operationalize with caching/batching.

Mateo — I'll share the smoke sim CSV in the next hour and then let's aim to send the 1–2 page MAP packet to Jordan by EOD 6/5.

Ben Carter
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
